newsitem.title: UK: UK Northern Electric strategy flawed - bidder.
newsitem.headline: UK Northern Electric strategy flawed - bidder.

text.p: The reported strategy by beleagered British utility Northern Electric of selling off retail units to fight off a hostile bid is flawed and "insignificant," a spokesman for bidder CE Electric said.

"The (Sunday) newspapers are reporting that Northern is hoping to sell off 50 retail units and pay a special dividend," the spokesman told Reuters. "We don't know if this is true. But if it is, the effect will be insignificant."
The British Observer newspaper report said Northern's retail outlets, which include 11 out-of-town superstores, had a turnover of 54 million stg last year.

But the CE Electric spokesman said the retail outlets made only around 3.5 million stg last year. "They are a very small part of the business. It is not a particularly powerful platform for their defense."
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by U.S. energy group CalEnergy, is the British bid vehicle for Northern. It already owns some 29.45 percent of the company.
The Observer report said the sale of shops could help to fund an extra bonus payout to Northern's shareholders, but the spokesman said that proposal "stretches credibility."
"What will happen to the company's gearing? How can they justify it? It could severely stretch the company or even put it at risk," he added.
The Observer paper also said Northern Electric had admitted it was in very serious discussions with a white knight "whose identity has not been revealed."
"There is a strong possibility it is New Orleans-based utility Entergy," the paper said.

Entergy Corp is known to have tried a deal with London Electricity, which failed, but it is still looking for a UK presence. It already has a joint venture with British Petroleum to build a power plant in Hull, the paper noted.
Northern could not be reached for comment.
On Friday, following six-month results, Northern challenged CE Electric to raise its offer of 630 pence per share, but the bidder described the figures as "lacklustre" and below expectations.
Northern publishes its final defence document in two weeks time, and is expected to point out other "hidden assets" in the hope of achieving a better price for the company.
